subject: SLA-aware idle vs burst capacity split — traffic + sizing clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Liang <alex@graymatter.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — initial traffic snapshot and SLA question

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're excited to move toward a reserved/dedicated footprint for our conversational routing features. Two quick things to help your sizing:

- Attached is a short traffic sample for one weekday (CSV): per-minute request counts, average prompt tokens, average response tokens.
- Our product team expects a steady baseline of ~150 qps across the US during business hours, with short bursts up to ~2.5k qps for 1–3 minute windows during marketing events.

What's unclear for us is how Redwood treats "idle capacity" vs. "burst pool" from an SLA perspective. If we commit to N GPUs, how much headroom do you reserve for burst routing vs. how much is 'best-effort' and could be preempted? Our legal team will need clear language on guaranteed concurrency and fallback behavior for the contract.

Can you send a quick questionnaire so we can give you the right distributions (prompt/response lengths, concurrency targets, acceptable tail latency) for sizing? Also attaching "sla_expectations.docx" with our drafter's priorities.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Engineering, GrayMatter AI

Attachments: graymatter_traffic_sample.csv (CSV, 120k rows), sla_expectations.docx (DOCX, 12KB)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Liang <alex@graymatter.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial traffic snapshot and SLA question

Hi Alex — great to hear. Appreciate the sample and the SLA doc; I've read through both. Quick checklist below to make sure our sizing model and contract language line up. If you can fill these out (or confirm the numbers in the CSV), we can produce a committed-GPU plan with a proposed burst-policy and a clear non-preemption guarantee for the committed capacity.

Redwood sizing questionnaire (short form) — please reply inline or attach a filled copy:

1) Peak and baseline
   - Baseline sustained qps (business hours): confirm 150 qps?
   - Peak burst qps: confirm target 2.5k qps and typical burst duration (you mentioned 1–3 minutes)

2) Prompt/response lengths (per request averages)
   - Avg prompt tokens: (CSV column: prompt_tokens)
   - Avg response tokens: (CSV column: response_tokens)
   - 95th percentile response tokens: (helps with GPU padding)

3) Session shape and tails
   - Fraction of requests that are single-turn vs multi-turn (avg turns per session)
   - Desired p99 latency SLO for interactive calls (e.g., 250ms end-to-end token latency)

4) SLA priorities
   - Which is more critical: latency SLO or sustained throughput during bursts?
   - Acceptable fallback: queueing up to X seconds, degrade to smaller model, or reject traffic?

5) Regional routing
   - Will you require strictly-US routing? Any EU/APAC users expected in year 1?

6) Cost guardrails and oversubscription
   - Do you have a maximum acceptable oversubscription ratio for committed pool (e.g., 1.2x baseline)?

Notes on idle vs burst: Our committed fleet guarantees reserved GPU capacity that will not be preempted for other customers. We typically recommend carving an explicit burst pool (reserved but elastic within the committed contract) so you have predictable latency for baseline and a documented burst headroom for events. The remainder of extra burst capacity can be served from a best-effort overflow (hosted spare capacity) with documented fallbacks. We'll provide proposed contract language once we have the workload shape.

I'll loop Karthik for GPU-mix guidance and Marissa for contract guardrails in the next message.

Best,
Camila
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft_questionnaire.csv (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-24T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial traffic snapshot and SLA question

Camila / Karthik — quick internal note before we send the sizing guidance to Alex:

- If GrayMatter's 150 qps baseline is accurate, we should propose a conservative oversubscription of 1.1x for baseline (to reduce cost) but carve a locked-in burst pool equal to ~40% of their projected peak (i.e., ~1k qps) as part of the committed footprint. That provides deterministic service for most events and pushes the remaining envelope to best-effort.
- For their 2.5k qps short bursts, advise a GPU mix: 70% A100-80GB equivalents (for large-context chat) + 30% T4-like instances for short, cheap inference paths and batching.
- Contract language: explicit definition of "burst pool" (minutes of elasticity), "overflow policy" (best-effort with documented fallbacks), and a p99 latency measurement window.

I'll draft the suggested numbers once Camila gets the 95th token percentiles and session-turn distribution.

-Marissa
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Liang <alex@graymatter.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@graymatter.ai
Date: 2027-05-26T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial traffic snapshot and SLA question

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few follow-ups and an ask: could you confirm the CSV columns below and provide the 95th percentile response length? If you prefer, we can take your CSV and return a populated sizing worksheet.

Required fields in the CSV (if missing, please add):
- timestamp_minute, requests, prompt_tokens_avg, response_tokens_avg, response_tokens_p95, avg_session_turns

Questionnaire answers we've captured so far (please confirm):
- Baseline: 150 qps (09:00–18:00 PT weekdays)
- Peak burst: 2.5k qps for 1–3 minutes during events
- Prompt tokens (avg): 28
- Response tokens (avg): 120
- Response tokens (p95): -- please provide (missing from CSV)
- Session shape: ~30% multi-turn, avg 3 turns per session
- Desired interactive p99 token latency: 300ms (client expectation)
- Region: US-only year 1
- Oversubscription tolerance: up to 1.15x for baseline, but want a locked burst pool for events

Next steps:
1) If you can reply with response_tokens_p95, we will run a GPU-pool sizing simulation and return: recommended committed GPU count, burst pool size, suggested GPU mix, and sample contract language for the burst and overflow behaviors.
2) If legal wants earlier draft language, loop in your procurement contact (I included procurement@graymatter.ai).

Thanks — target to have a sizing proposal back to you within 3 business days after we get the p95.

Best,
Camila
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Inline: Forwarded traffic CSV included (graymatter_traffic_sample.csv).
